strengths: Addresses a fundamental systems bottleneck in 3D equivariant graph neural networks by eliminating the explicit materialization of high-dimensional edge tensors, achieving O(|V|) activation memory scaling.

Sound mathematical formulation with clear proofs in the appendices; Proposition 4.3 and Lemma 4.1 rigorously establish how SO(2) axis-alignment induces parity-dependent sparsity in real SO(3) spherical harmonic representations.
Substantial speedup and memory improvements in practice: scales comfortably to 100k atoms where mainstream baselines (MACE-Large, EquiformerV2, eSCN) face out-of-memory errors beyond 10k–50k atoms.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation covering standard quantum-chemical datasets (SPICE, OMol25, OC20) as well as practical molecular dynamics benchmarks (liquid water RDF and 30k-atom solvated protein simulation).
weaknesses: The abstract ends abruptly with an incomplete sentence ('Our released code can be found at ' without a link or repository placeholder).

There is a slight discrepancy in the presentation of the attention mechanism between the main text (Equations 6–7) and Appendix D (Equations 34–35, which incorporate an additional edge feature Fea_ij); this should be harmonized or explicitly reconciled in the main text.

The paper focuses primarily on the forward pass algorithm (Algorithm 1) and forward benchmarks, but conservative force prediction requires backpropagating through the potential. Further discussion of the backward kernel implementation and memory overhead during gradient computation would strengthen the manuscript.

strengths: Addresses a critical and timely bottleneck in equivariant graph neural networks: the high memory footprint and latency caused by explicitly materializing O(|E|) intermediate edge tensors in high-bandwidth memory (HBM).

Sound algebraic formulation: Equivariant Axis-Aligned Sparsification (EAAS) elegantly uses the pole sparsity of spherical harmonics (Lemma 4.1) under an SO(3) -> SO(2) frame alignment to collapse dense Clebsch-Gordan contractions into sparse, deterministic parity-based re-indexing (Proposition 4.3).

Hardware-aware execution: Implements an on-the-fly streaming attention aggregation kernel in Triton with online softmax, effectively reducing the activation memory complexity from O(|E|) to O(|V|) and avoiding intermediate edge materialization.

Extensive empirical validation across multiple dimensions: strong accuracy on SPICE and OMol25 benchmarks matching or outperforming state-of-the-art baselines; rigorous microbenchmarking against cuEquivariance and OpenEquivariance; impressive scaling up to 100,000 atoms on a single GPU without out-of-memory errors; and real-world validation via molecular dynamics simulations on liquid water and a ~30k-atom protein system.
weaknesses: Algorithmic novelty builds heavily on existing foundations: the mathematical node-centric expansion relies directly on the binomial decomposition introduced in E2Former-V1 (Li et al., 2025), and SO(2) axis-alignment is conceptually related to approaches used in eSCN and EquiformerV2, although its combination with node-centric recoupling and kernel fusion is well-executed.

Details on the backward pass and training efficiency are relatively sparse: while Algorithm 1 outlines the forward pass and Table 9 mentions conservative force training (requiring differentiation through energy, F = -∇E), the paper primarily focuses on inference throughput. Clarification on the backward pass implementation in Triton and training memory overhead would strengthen the presentation.
Minor presentation oversight: the Abstract ends with an incomplete sentence ('Our released code can be found at') with the repository link missing.

MD simulation analysis is limited in scope: the protein refinement experiment is run for only 2 ns on a single target, which provides limited statistical evidence for long-term conformational stability across diverse biomolecular systems.

strengths: Addresses a fundamental, critical bottleneck in equivariant neural networks: the memory wall and high I/O overhead caused by explicit edge-level tensor materialization in graphs.

Hardware-aware design that effectively translates the theoretical node-centric factorization of E2Former into practical speedups via an on-the-fly streaming reduction (Algorithm 1) implemented in a fused Triton kernel, reducing activation memory to O(|V|).

Impressive empirical throughput and scalability: enables inference on systems with up to 100k atoms on a single GPU without out-of-memory (OOM) errors, where mainstream equivariant baselines (e.g., MACE, EquiformerV2) fail beyond 10k-50k atoms.

Competitive predictive accuracy across standard molecular and materials benchmarks (SPICE, OMol25, and OC20 S2EF-2M), accompanied by practical MD validation on bulk water and a 30k-atom solvated protein system.

Thorough performance benchmarks and ablations against established libraries (e3nn, cuEquivariance, OpenEquivariance), clearly demonstrating structural latency and memory benefits across neighbor densities and system sizes.
weaknesses: Incremental algorithmic novelty over E2Former-V1 and eSCN: the node-centric algebraic factorization is largely inherited from E2Former-V1 (Li et al., 2025), and exploiting pole sparsity via z-axis rotation to reduce SO(3) to SO(2) is conceptually very similar to the mechanism in eSCN (Passaro & Zitnick, 2023).
A drafting oversight in the abstract: the last sentence ends abruptly with 'Our released code can be found at ' without a link or repository placeholder.

MD simulations are relatively brief (2 ns for the solvated protein, single RDF curve for water). Evaluating longer trajectories and thermodynamic observables (e.g., diffusion coefficients, density fluctuations) would provide more definitive proof of stability and physical fidelity.

The formulation relies on moving non-linearities out of the equivariant value path and into the scalar attention scores (Appendix D) to facilitate fused execution; while accuracy on the tested benchmarks is maintained, further discussion or analysis on whether this trade-off impairs expressivity in more complex tensor-property prediction tasks would strengthen the paper.

strengths: Addresses a fundamental bottleneck in equivariant graph neural networks: the high memory footprint and memory-bandwidth saturation caused by explicitly materializing edge-level tensors and dense Clebsch-Gordan contractions.

The proposed Equivariant Axis-Aligned Sparsification (EAAS) effectively unifies the node-centric coordinate factorization of E2Former with SO(2) frame alignment, transforming dense tensor contractions into efficient, sparse parity-dependent re-indexing rules.

Significant system-level improvements: the on-the-fly streaming attention kernel achieves up to ~20x speedup in TFLOPS over naive PyTorch implementations and enables scaling up to 100,000 atoms on a single GPU without out-of-memory (OOM) failures.

Thorough empirical evaluation across standard and foundation-scale benchmarks (SPICE, OMol25), demonstrating that the substantial computational and memory gains come without degradation in energy and force prediction accuracy.
Includes physical validation via molecular dynamics simulations on bulk water, demonstrating stable dynamics and faithful reproduction of experimental radial distribution functions.
weaknesses: Conceptual novelty is somewhat incremental: the core algorithmic ideas largely integrate existing paradigms, specifically eSCN's SO(3)->SO(2) alignment, E2Former's binomial recoupling factorization, and FlashAttention's online softmax.

Discrepancy in the presentation of kernel fusion: Section 4.4 and Algorithm 1 present a single, fully fused streaming kernel that avoids materializing scores or attention weights using online softmax. However, the reference code snippet in Appendix A (page 11) breaks the computation into two separate kernels (`triton_sparse_qk` and `triton_sparse_v`) with an intermediate `alpha = softmax(scores, dim=1)` tensor of shape N x K x H. The authors should clarify whether the evaluated implementation is fully fused or two-stage.

Limited discussion and implementation details regarding the backward pass. While 'linear activation memory' is a central claim, Algorithm 1 only describes the forward pass. FlashAttention-style benefits during training rely on recomputing attention scores during the backward pass; details on backward kernel implementation, recomputation overhead, and training memory benchmarks should be elaborated.

The baseline comparison in Figure 1 uses PyTorch's `scaled_dot_product_attention` with a materialized N x N mask as the 'FlashAttention' baseline. For graph data where |E| = O(kN), evaluating an N x N dense mask inherently incurs quadratic overhead O(N^2), making it an unnatural baseline compared to optimized sparse message-passing frameworks.
Minor presentation issues, including an incomplete sentence and typo in the abstract ('The code is avalible at ').

strengths: Addresses an important and practical bottleneck in 3D equivariant neural networks: the severe memory and computational overhead of edge-centric tensor products and explicit edge activations.

The theoretical derivation of Equivariant Axis-Aligned Sparsification (EAAS) in Section 4.3 and Appendix B is mathematically sound, cleanly demonstrating how pole alignment reduces dense Clebsch-Gordan contractions to sparse, parity-dependent re-indexing.
Achieves impressive inference scalability up to 100,000 atoms (Table 3), running where traditional equivariant transformers suffer from out-of-memory (OOM) failures.

Solid empirical performance on standard molecular modeling benchmarks, achieving competitive or superior MAE on SPICE and OMol25, and matching bulk water radial distribution functions in MD simulations.
weaknesses: Contradiction between the claimed fused kernel and the implementation sketch in Appendix A: Algorithm 1 describes a fully fused on-the-fly streaming attention with online softmax that avoids materializing $O(|E|)$ edge tensors. However, Appendix A's code sketch (`Reference implementation snippets`) shows two separate Triton kernels (`triton_sparse_qk` and `triton_sparse_v`) with PyTorch `softmax` in between, which explicitly materializes intermediate tensors of shape $N \times K \times H$. This directly contradicts the core claim of avoiding $O(|E|)$ materialization in the benchmarked pipeline.

Unsubstantiated claims regarding training efficiency: The abstract and contribution list assert that the model enables efficient training of large equivariant transformers and significantly outperforms baselines in training throughput. However, all throughput, latency, and memory experiments in Section 5 and Table 3 only benchmark inference and forward passes; no backward pass latency, training memory, or training throughput numbers are provided.

Incremental originality over prior work: The core algebraic trick of EAAS (rotating to align the z-axis to make spherical harmonics sparse at $m=0$) is directly borrowed from eSCN (Passaro & Zitnick, 2023), applied here to the node-centric recoupling formula of E2Former (Li et al., 2025).

Missing details and incomplete presentation: The code link in the abstract is broken/empty ('The code is avalible at \n 1. Introduction'), and typographical errors remain in the manuscript (e.g., 'avalible', 'tow datasets'). Furthermore, in Table 1, subset breakdowns for eSEN are missing without explanation.

strengths: Addressing the memory footprint and latency bottlenecks of equivariant graph neural networks by integrating algebraic sparsification with hardware-aware GPU kernels is an important and practically relevant research direction.

The empirical evaluation is comprehensive in scope, spanning diverse benchmarks including SPICE, OMol25, large-scale inference throughput stress-testing up to 100,000 atoms, and bulk water molecular dynamics simulations.
weaknesses: Mathematical inconsistency and failure of translational invariance: In Section 4.2 (Eq. 8–10), the authors claim to realize the factorized message passing of E2Former (Eq. 5). However, Eq. 5 fundamentally relies on the binomial local expansion of solid spherical harmonics combined with Wigner-6j recoupling, summing over degrees u ∈ {0, ..., ℓ} to ensure the arbitrary coordinate origin algebraically cancels out. In Eq. 8–10, the authors drop the binomial expansion, the summation over u, and the 6j recoupling entirely, replacing it with a simple two-stage tensor product: h'_j = h_j ⊗ R(r_j) and h_hat_i = m_i ⊗ R(r_i). Because solid spherical harmonics R(r) evaluated at absolute positions depend on the global origin, this formulation breaks Euclidean translation invariance. Furthermore, while the paper repeatedly claims to 'unify Wigner-6j recoupling with SO(2) sparsification' (Abstract, Section 1, Section 4.1), no 6j recoupling is ever treated or derived in Section 4.3 or Appendix B; the derivations strictly concern standard Clebsch–Gordan tensor products.

Contradiction between algorithmic claims and reference implementation: A central contribution of the paper (Section 4.4, Algorithm 1) is an on-the-fly fused Triton kernel that avoids materializing edge-level intermediate tensors via online streaming softmax. However, in Appendix A ('Reference implementation snippets'), the explicit code snippet provided for 'Ours' directly contradicts this claim: it computes scores via 'triton_sparse_qk' (producing an explicit tensor of shape N x K x H), performs a global PyTorch 'softmax(scores, dim=1)' (materializing alpha of shape N x K x H in HBM), and then feeds alpha into 'triton_sparse_v'. The claimed fully fused, edge-free streaming execution is not reflected in the provided implementation.

Fundamentally flawed baseline in scaling comparisons: In Figure 1 and Appendix A, the 'FlashAttention' baseline is implemented using PyTorch's scaled_dot_product_attention with a pre-built N x N dense mask ('mask = build_mask_from_idx(idx)'). Consequently, this baseline executes an O(N^2) dense attention computation (e.g., allocating a ~1 GB mask and ~10^9 operations at N = 32,768). In contrast, the proposed method evaluates a sparse neighbor graph with fixed K = 64, which scales as O(NK). Comparing an O(NK) sparse gather against an O(N^2) masked attention baseline to claim superior algorithmic scaling with N is ungrounded and misleading.

Limited novelty of EAAS over existing literature: The algebraic core of EAAS (Section 4.3 and Appendix B)—aligning the frame to the z-axis so that spherical harmonics collapse to m = 0, thereby reducing Clebsch–Gordan contractions to parity-dependent sparse re-indexing—is mathematically identical to the SO(3) -> SO(2) reduction introduced by eSCN (Passaro & Zitnick, ICML 2023) and utilized in EquiformerV2 (Liao et al., 2023). Presenting this known reduction as a novel contribution overstates originality.

Direct reporting contradiction on OMol25: In Section 5.3, the text states that 'the conservative variant achieves an aggregate Energy MAE of 1.27 meV/atom, matching eSEN-small and significantly outperforming UMA-S (3.62 meV/atom)'. However, Table 2 clearly reports the Total Energy MAE for E2V2-Cons as 2.09 meV/atom, while 1.27 meV/atom belongs to the competitor eSEN-sm-cons. Citing the competitor's superior score as the proposed model's own performance in the text is a critical discrepancy.

Presentation and attribution deficiencies: The paper exhibits multiple careless drafting issues, including an incomplete sentence with a missing repository link on Page 1 ('The code is avalible at 
 1. Introduction'), recurring attribution errors conflating eSEN (Fu et al., 2025) with eSCN (Passaro & Zitnick, 2023) in both the text and references, and typographical errors ('avalible', 'tow datasets').
